T HE S TRUCTURE T HEOREM Our main structure theorem states that for any set of k interior disjoint rectangles in the plane there is a constant fraction size subset with respect to which there exists a nearly perfect CCR-partition. We state the theorem here and we utilize it for the algorithm in the next section; the proof of the structure theorem is given in Section V. While Conjecture 1 remains open, and if true would imply a constant-factor approximation for MISR (via dynamic programming), our structural result suffices for obtaining a constant factor approximation (Theorem IV.1), which is 342 First, we consider the set I 0 of maximal expansions, as described previously, of the k input rectangles I = {R1 , . . . , Rk } within B. Recall that, appealing to Observation 1, the set I 0 is the disjoint union of subsets: I 0 = Ih ∪ Iv ∪ I0 , where Ih is the subset of “red” rectangles that are nested horizontally, Iv is the subset of “blue” rectangles that are nested vertically, and I0 is the subset of “gray” rectangles that are not nested on any of their four sides. Refer to Figure 3. It cannot be that both |Ih | and |Iv | are greater than k/2; thus, assume, without loss of generality, that |Ih | ≤ k/2. Then, there are |Iv | + |I0 | ≥ k/2 “non-red” rectangles.2 We now describe a process by which a subset of Ω(k) of the rectangles of I 0 is chosen, and a CCR-partition, Π, is constructed that is nearly perfect with respect to this subset, and, thus, by the following claim, is nearly perfect with respect to the corresponding subset of (sub-)rectangles I.
